factors.s: This is where conditions bite hardest, and GridIron now applies it to every projection. Fitted continuously on 3,424 team-games against each team’s own leave-one-out baseline, so a windy stadium’s run-heavy habits cannot masquerade as weather: each mph of sustained wind above 8 costs 0.13 pass attempts (t = −2.7) and 0.05 yards per attempt (t = −4.6), and every 10°F below 45 costs a further 0.16 yards per attempt (t = −2.4). Indoors adds 0.10 yards per carry. One caution that halves most published weather effects: these are fitted on SUSTAINED wind, not gusts — gusts run roughly 1.8x higher, and using them here would double the penalty.

The same conditions barely move game totals, and the market prices them. GridIron adds no conditions adjustment to its totals: hand-set adjustments left held-out error unchanged (10.328 vs 10.329 with none) and adjustments fitted on 2019-22 made it worse (10.393). The learning loop re-tests this every week.

Real in raw results: a venue measured 4 points friendlier than average predicts about +1.6 points of home margin. But the team ratings already absorb it — adding per-venue edges on top barely moved held-out 2023-25 margin error (10.271 vs 10.272), far short of earning a weight, so GridIron uses one flat 1.2-point edge, and none at neutral sites. The learning loop re-tests a venue edge every week; it has to earn its weight.

The one factor that is genuinely empty. A crew’s career scoring average has no measurable relationship to the next game’s total — correlation −0.02 against the market and against a raw baseline alike. A 17-game sample has a ±3-point standard error, so a crew that looks 8 points off league average is almost certainly just noise. Read the crew name on a card as trivia.
Nothing detectable. Visiting teams gain 338 yards at Mile High against 353 everywhere else — a 15-yard gap with a ±24-yard error bar across 59 games. The reputation is not visible in the production.

Buffalo, Cleveland, San Francisco and Kansas City each suppress visiting offense by more than 30 yards, and Detroit inflates it by 49. But those are the defenses those teams fielded, not the buildings. Treat any raw venue ranking as a defense ranking wearing a disguise.
Home teams off 3+ extra days go over the total by 1.7 points — the only rest effect that clears its own error bar, and it clears it barely.

blend.note: GridIron gets 15% of the blended line; the learning loop re-tests that share every week against the closing line alone.

track.note_scope: Two different questions get asked of every factor here: does it change what happens on the field, and does it beat the price. A factor can be emphatically yes on the first and no on the second.

qb.s: A backup under centre is worth 3.9 points of margin, fitted on 2019-22. A starter counts as the usual one when he has the most starts so far this season — all anyone can know at kickoff. On the 245 held-out 2023-25 games that involved a backup, the term cut GridIron’s margin error from 10.23 to 10.16; the learning loop re-tests its size every week. An offseason quarterback change carried no measurable direction in week 1, so GridIron applies nothing for it and simply flags it.

track.asof: Each game is predicted by the weights in force before its week (weights version 1).

wxfit.note: Fitted on 3,424 team-games 2019-2025 against each team’s own leave-one-out baseline, using sustained wind. Effects are expressed relative to average fitted conditions, which is identical to the fitted intercept: projections come from all-weather history, so a calm outdoor game sits slightly above them.

injrule.note: Players ruled Out, Doubtful or on IR are projected at zero and their volume is handed to teammates using rates measured on 2025 absences: receiving disperses across the position group, rushing concentrates on the next back. Only 75% of lost targets and 54% of lost carries are recovered at all — the rest is volume that simply never happens.

test.how: each season fitted only on earlier seasons; [certain to play, with the discount]; p = week-clustered bootstrap share with no improvement

q.note: Questionable players are projected for the share of games players in the same spot have actually played since 2019 (2962 reports), and for lighter use when they do play; the rest of their simulations score zero.

props.note: GridIron leans under on 0% of these lines. Its distributions are well calibrated against actual results (48.2% of outcomes land below the predicted median across 2,301 validated player-weeks), so this is a real disagreement with the book rather than a modelling artefact — but books are known to shade player-prop overs, and without historical prop lines there is no way to prove which side is right. Treat the raw lean as unproven. The relative column strips out GridIron’s own average lean so you can see which players it disagrees on specifically. No prices are published with these lines, so break-even is assumed at -110.

live.note: every play predicted by the live weights in force at its week, from the pregame numbers GridIron showed
